About the Opportunity

OKX is hiring a Senior Compliance Manager to build and run our global derivatives trade and transaction reporting function. The function covers CFTC swap data reporting under Part 45, EU transaction reporting under MiFIR, EU derivatives reporting under EMIR, UK MiFIR and UK EMIR, and ASIC derivative transaction reporting across multiple OKX entities and a growing derivatives product set. These regimes have different scopes, reporting parties, data requirements and destinations. You will determine how they apply to OKX’s activities and help build a reliable process for meeting each obligation.

Most of the work is data and judgment: deciding what is reportable, by which entity, and to whom, then making sure the right trade and lifecycle data reaches the right swap data repository, trade repository, or regulator on time and reconciles to our trading records. You will own reporting scoping/eligibility, submission monitoring, and the controls that show our reports are complete, accurate, and timely.

This is a hands-on Compliance leadership role. You will work with Trading, Product, Engineering, Data, Legal, local Compliance teams and reporting providers, and you will lead regulatory change in this space. Responsibilities for source data, systems, submissions and remediation will be agreed across those teams; you will lead the compliance framework and stay close enough to the process to identify and proactively resolve problems. You will report to the Head of Markets and Product Compliance and support a central function that owns reporting interpretation, scoping, oversight, and remediation for every entity in scope.

What You’ll Be Doing

•

Interpret and apply derivatives and transaction reporting rules across global regimes, including CFTC Part 45, MiFIR Article 26, EMIR Article 9, UK MiFIR, UK EMIR, and the ASIC Derivative Transaction Rules (Reporting) 2024, exercising independent technical judgment, supported by Legal and outside counsel.

•

Own and maintain entity, product, and transaction-level reporting scoping and eligibility: which entity reports, which products and lifecycle events are in scope, which counterparty role triggers the obligation, and which repository or authority receives the report.

•

Oversee, support, and help maintain the daily reporting process. Monitor submissions against deadlines, including T+1 for MiFIR transaction reports, investigate rejections and breaks, and track each one to resolution.

•

Reconcile reported activity to trading records and repository data, and coordinate corrections and back-reporting with the teams that own the relevant systems and data.

•

Define and maintain the reporting data specification with Engineering and Data, including field-level mapping, reference data such as LEIs, UTIs, UPIs, and ISINs, and the validation rules applied before submission.

•

Build and run the control framework: completeness, accuracy, and timeliness checks, exception management, management information, and records that hold up to regulator and audit review.

•

Drive reporting readiness and remediation. Assess new derivatives products, new entities, and regulatory changes, identify control gaps, agree on owners and deadlines across Compliance, Operations, Product, and Engineering, and track delivery.

•

Escalate material issues. Assess the impact of reporting errors, escalate to senior management, and support notifications to regulators where required.

•

Manage relationships with swap data repositories, trade repositories, approved reporting mechanisms, and reporting vendors, including onboarding, testing, and service issues.

•

Hands-on leader. Build a small team, and coordinate with and train local compliance leads.

•

Support independent testing by Compliance Monitoring, Risk, and Internal Audit, and support regulator inquiries with complete, reproducible records.

What We Look For In You

•

A degree in finance, economics, law, data science, or computer science, or an equivalent professional qualification

•

7+ years in trade reporting, transaction reporting, or regulatory reporting at an exchange, broker, bank, trading firm, fintech, or digital asset platform

•

Deep working knowledge of at least two of the following regimes: CFTC swap data reporting, MiFIR transaction reporting, EMIR, UK MiFIR, UK EMIR, and ASIC derivative transaction reporting. Hands-on experience with both a US and a European regime is strongly preferred.

•

A sound understanding of derivatives trade lifecycles and the data needed to report executions, changes, terminations and, where applicable, valuations and collateral.

•

The ability to interrogate large datasets, investigate reporting breaks and explain clear requirements to engineers and other business partners. SQL or comparable data analysis skills are highly desirable.

•

Experience building or improving a reporting framework, including procedures, reconciliations, exception management and evidence that can withstand regulatory or audit scrutiny; this may include remediating historical reporting errors, including back-reporting.

•

The judgment to make proportionate risk decisions, escalate material issues and lead delivery across teams without relying on a single team to own every part of the reporting process.

•

Experience with digital asset derivatives, such as perpetual futures and options, and how they map to reporting product classifications

Experience leading a regulatory reporting change program, such as EMIR Refit, UK EMIR Refit, the CFTC reporting rewrite, or the ASIC 2024 rules.

Familiarity with ISO 20022 XML reporting formats.

Why this role matters

As an Information Security Risk Manager, you will play a key role in shaping a structured, data-driven approach to information security risk management at Exness, helping the business make better decisions through quantitative risk analysis.

Every year, Exness makes dozens of high-value security and technology decisions involving millions of dollars — from security investments and vendor selection to architecture changes, cyber insurance, and release readiness.

Your focus will be on quantifying uncertainty to support these decisions, moving beyond traditional risk registers, 5x5 risk matrices, and heat maps towards evidence-based financial risk modelling.

We are looking for someone who can demonstrate the financial impact of different options. For example: "Option A reduces our 1-in-20-year loss from $8M to $3M for $400K. Option B costs half as much but leaves the tail almost unchanged."

The ideal candidate is an experienced, hands-on risk management professional with strong analytical capabilities, able to work independently, influence stakeholders, and translate complex risk scenarios into actionable business insights.

The role is based in our Limassol office, Cyprus. In case of relocation, we offer full relocation support for you and your family to make your move smooth and worry-free.

What you'll actually do

• Support specific decisions. Build quantitative models for security investments, architecture and infrastructure changes, third-party onboarding and incident response capacity.

• Model uncertainty properly. Use probability distributions, Monte Carlo simulation and loss exceedance curves instead of single-point estimates or ordinal scores. Aggregate risks by simulation, not by adding scores.

• Combine internal incident data, technical security assessment results, industry loss data, threat intelligence and calibrated expert estimates. Update the models with Bayesian methods as new evidence arrives.

• Run cost-benefit analysis and value-of-information analysis on alternative controls, including "do nothing" and "accept the risk and insure it."

• Embed analysis in existing processes. Build risk analysis into change management, architecture review, procurement and budgeting, so it happens inside the decisions people already make. It should not become a separate risk process.

• Make metrics risk-aware. Add uncertainty ranges and leading indicators to existing operational and security KPIs instead of building a standalone KRI catalogue.

• Present findings to senior leadership as decision trade-offs: ranges, probabilities and money.

• Produce regulatory and audit documentation as a by-product of the decision analysis, with minimal extra effort.

• Partner with IT, Information Security, and risk owners to define risk treatment plans, evaluate control effectiveness, and monitor remediation activities

• Collaborate with stakeholders across the organisation to promote consistent risk management practices, strengthen risk ownership, and improve risk awareness

Who we’re looking for

• Proven ability to influence business decisions through quantitative risk analysis, with 2–3 examples of how the analysis impacted budget, vendor, architecture, or go/no-go decisions and their outcomes.

• Strong understanding of probability distributions, Monte Carlo simulation, sensitivity analysis, and basic Bayesian reasoning.

• Practical experience with Python, R, or spreadsheet simulation tools such as SIPmath or ModelRisk.

• Solid understanding of infrastructure, cloud, application security, and attack paths, enabling effective collaboration with engineers and Information Security SMEs.

• Strong quantitative foundation, ideally supported by a degree in Mathematics, Statistics, Engineering, Economics, or a related field.

• Familiarity with FAIR or a similar approach is a plus, with greater emphasis on mathematical understanding than formal certification.

• Ability to explain complex quantitative concepts, such as loss exceedance curves, clearly and concisely to senior leadership.

• Ability to challenge established practices constructively, using evidence and well-reasoned alternatives.

• Excellent communication and stakeholder management skills, with the ability to translate complex risk assessments into actionable recommendations for technical and non-technical audiences, including senior leadership.

• Experience in fintech, financial services or other regulated, high-availability environments

Kraken is seeking a Senior Risk Analyst to join the Security Governance, Risk, and Compliance (SecGRC) team. Reporting to the Senior Manager of Security Risk Management, this role is a key contributor to the execution and maturation of Kraken's Security Risk Management program. You'll conduct rigorous risk assessments, produce high-quality analysis, and help build the operational infrastructure that makes the program run — all in close partnership with program leadership. This role offers the opportunity to make a meaningful and lasting impact both within Kraken and across the broader industry.

The ideal candidate is deeply analytical, process-minded, and energized by turning ambiguous risk signals into clear, repeatable, and scalable workflows. Entrepreneurial spirit and comfort with iterating quickly is a must. This is a fully remote role.




THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Execute security risk assessments end-to-end — scoping, data gathering, analysis, findings documentation, and communicating results to stakeholders — in alignment with program methodology set by leadership

 - Support the development and continuous refinement of risk assessment templates, workflows, and process guides that make the program consistent and scalable

 - Maintain risk registers and ensure identified risks are tracked accurately and progressing through mitigation, remediation, or acceptance workflows

 - Assist in building and maintaining Key Risk Indicators (KRI) tracking and risk reporting outputs, translating raw data into clear, well-structured deliverables for review by senior leadership

 - Partner with technical teams including Vulnerability Management, Application Security, and Blue Team to gather risk-relevant data and incorporate operational findings into assessment work

 - Identify opportunities to streamline and automate risk processes and bring those recommendations to program leadership for prioritization

 - Contribute to the documentation and upkeep of risk program standards, procedures, and guidance materials

 - Collaborate with cross-functional teams including Compliance, Internal Audit, Engineering, and Legal to ensure risk findings are well-contextualized and properly actioned

 - Support audit preparedness activities and risk-related reporting as directed by program leadership




WHAT YOU BRING

 - 5+ years of experience in information security risk management, cybersecurity governance, or GRC

 - Hands-on experience conducting risk assessments and owning findings documentation — not just supporting assessments, but running them

 - Strong working knowledge of risk management frameworks such as NIST CSF, ISO 27005, PCI DSS, or DoCRA

 - Demonstrated ability to build repeatable processes — you've taken something ad hoc and made it structured and scalable

 - Strong data analysis skills; able to clean, interpret, and present risk data clearly and accurately

 - Experience contributing to KRI tracking and risk reporting for internal stakeholder audiences

 - Familiarity with GRC tools such as AuditBoard, Archer, OneTrust, or ServiceNow GRC

 - Proficient in Google Workspace; SQL and/or Tableau experience a strong plus

 - Excellent written communication — your deliverables are clear, well-organized, and don't require heavy editing

 - Self-directed and comfortable operating in ambiguity; you take direction well and run with it

 - Bachelor's degree or above in IT, Cybersecurity, Business Administration, Engineering, or a related field

 - CISM, CRISC, or ISO 27001 credentials a plus; experience in fintech or regulated industries preferred

Consumer Growth builds mobile and web experiences that help people become Kraken customers, fund their accounts, invest, earn, access new products, build wealth and stay lifelong clients. Product, engineering, design, data, and lifecycle marketing build together.




THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own growth in viral, KOL- and creator-referred new transacting users (NTUs). Set aggressive NTU targets backed by a credible growth model, then beat them. Build and scale sharing, referral, and creator systems that drive 10x, then 50x growth while hitting payback targets.

 - Build sharing people find useful. Create natural reasons to pass on product value, and referral programs with modeled payback incentives, and without relying on aggressive incentives to hit targets. Make both work for the sender, recipient, and business.

 - Own the audience-to-customer journey. Build and test paths from recommendations and creator audiences to product value and a first transaction. Partner with the teams that own onboarding and core product experiences on shared journeys.

 - Own Consumer features and updates for the KOL Platform. Set the Consumer roadmap, ship features and ongoing improvements, and make measurement and commercial tools trustworthy and easy to use. Work with the teams that own KOL and affiliate relationships.

 - Build creator tools across Kraken’s app and web. Help creators, key opinion leaders (KOLs), and power referrers invite their followers and turn their audiences into valuable new transacting customers. Understand their different motivations and build with core product teams.

 - Make acquisition economics work. Own acquisition cost and gross-margin payback against clear targets, including fully loaded incentive, partner, operating, and fraud costs. Use downstream retention and revenue to judge what deserves more investment.

 - Increase virality per new transacting user and per returning user. Test ways to improve send conversion, invites per sender, and invite-to-first-transaction conversion. Improve repeat sharing and loop speed, and prove the gains create incremental valuable new transacting customers.

 - Build measurement you can trust. Validate instrumentation, define hypotheses and guardrails, and run tests that can detect meaningful effects. Separate attributed activity from incremental growth, interpret uncertainty honestly, and check that gains persist as you scale.




WHAT YOU BRING

 - You’ve personally built a product, tool, feature, or experience that spread beyond its initial audience. You can explain why it spread, your contribution, and how it acquired valuable customers.

 - Repeated success beating acquisition targets through referrals, product virality, or creator-led growth. Show the baseline, target, result, timeframe, component rates you improved, and your personal contribution. Bring evidence the gains lasted.

 - Strong growth product sense. You understand sharing psychology and the different motivations of customers, creators, KOLs, and power referrers. You combine customer research, creative product instincts, and strong UX and copy to give people a reason to participate.

 - Analytical independence. You independently investigate behavior with SQL and product analytics, validate instrumentation, and build funnel, cohort, and growth models.

 - Experimentation and commercial judgment. You design reliable tests, interpret uncertainty honestly, and distinguish attribution from incremental growth. You understand acquisition cost and payback, including downstream retention, revenue, and fully loaded incentive and fraud costs.

 - Senior ownership and hands-on execution. You set strategy, make hard priority calls, align teams without relying on reporting lines, and deliver autonomously. You use AI and working prototypes to turn original ideas into experiences people can try.




NICE TO HAVES

 - Experience building self-service creator or affiliate tools, revenue-share systems, or reliable partner payouts.

 - Consumer fintech, crypto, payments, or experience designing financial promotions and fraud controls.

 - Experience adapting growth journeys across markets, cultures, and regulatory environments.

Enterprise Efficiency builds internal products and platforms that power how our company operates globally.

Turn HR domain expertise into effective products. Understand the policies, operational processes, and user needs across Payroll, Global Compensation, and Leave and Absence. Job Description
Campaign build, management and account health
•
Build, launch and maintain campaigns across Meta, TikTok and X for web conversion, lead generation, app install and app-event objectives.
•
Manage assigned campaigns and markets day to day, including objectives, optimisation events, audiences, placements, bids, budgets, schedules, creative, copy and destination settings.
•
Execute accurate campaign duplication, bulk changes and asset uploads using available platform tools and approved workflows.
•
Monitor delivery and diagnose issues including limited learning, low delivery, audience saturation, frequency pressure, placement inefficiency and conversion-signal weakness.
•
Maintain account hygiene through naming conventions, labels, URL and UTM checks, disapproval checks, pre-launch QA, change logs and routine health reviews.
•
Identify and implement optimisation opportunities independently within agreed commercial and compliance guardrails.
Audience strategy and analysis
•
Build and maintain prospecting, retargeting and lifecycle audience structures aligned to campaign objectives and customer journey stages.
•
Use approved first-party, website, app-engagement and platform audiences, including custom audiences, lookalike or equivalent expansion and automated audience products where appropriate.
•
Maintain accurate exclusions and suppression logic to reduce overlap, protect prospecting activity and avoid inappropriate retargeting.
•
Analyse audience performance by market, funnel stage, creative and placement; identify saturation, weak quality, scale constraints and expansion opportunities.
•
Turn audience findings into clear actions across targeting, exclusions, budget allocation, creative briefs and campaign structure.
Budget pacing and forecasting
•
Monitor spend against approved plans by platform, market and campaign, maintaining an accurate pacing view.
•
Flag over- or underspend risk early, explain the cause and recommend corrective action.
•
Reallocate budget within agreed guardrails based on performance, delivery opportunity, downstream quality and business priority.
•
Provide short-term forecasts and month-end outlooks, clearly stating assumptions and delivery risks.
•
Escalate material budget, tracking, policy or inventory constraints before they affect delivery.
Creative performance and briefing
•
Analyse performance by creative concept, hook, message, proposition, format, duration, placement, call to action and variation where data is available.
•
Identify winning and underperforming patterns, creative fatigue and gaps in platform-native asset coverage.
•
Convert findings into clear test hypotheses and prioritised recommendations rather than descriptive commentary.
•
Brief the creative team on new concepts, iterations and platform-native variations, including objective, audience, insight, hook, message, format, required versions and success metric.
•
Track assets from briefing through launch and post-test analysis, documenting learning for future iterations and localisation.
Landing-page and post-click performance
•
Monitor post-click conversion performance using available analytics, segmented by platform, campaign, audience, creative, device, market and landing page where useful.
•
Identify likely friction, message mismatch, weak journey alignment, broken links, tracking gaps or page-performance issues that may suppress conversion.
•
Check destination URLs, deep links, app-store routes, UTMs and campaign-to-page alignment as part of launch and ongoing QA.
•
Brief CRO, web, product or app teams on evidence-based improvement and testing opportunities; this role supports analysis and briefing rather than owning the full CRO roadmap or development.
Competitor monitoring
•
Monitor observable competitor advertising, messaging, offers, creative formats and landing-page approaches across priority markets.
•
Use public platform ad-transparency and creative-discovery resources, alongside market observations, to identify material shifts and testable themes.
•
Turn observations into practical recommendations for messaging, creative formats, audience hypotheses, landing pages or structured tests.
Structured testing
•
Maintain a prioritised test backlog across creative, audiences, placements, bidding and optimisation, campaign structures and landing pages.
•
Define a clear hypothesis, control and variant, primary success metric, guardrails and expected decision before launch.
•
Configure platform experiments or other agreed test designs, validate setup and protect data quality during the test.
•
Interpret results carefully, distinguishing directional evidence from conclusive findings and documenting limitations.
•
Record outcomes, decisions and next actions so learning can be reused across platforms and markets.
•
Support conversion-lift, brand-lift and incrementality studies through setup, QA and data collection under the direction of the paid social lead or measurement team.
Tracking and measurement - web and app
•
Maintain working knowledge of platform pixels/tags, event configuration and server-side or conversion API concepts relevant to Meta, TikTok and X.
•
Validate conversion events and diagnose broken, missing, duplicated or misfiring signals; deep engineering implementation remains with Analytics or MarTech.
•
Work with Analytics and MarTech partners on event mapping, data quality, attribution settings and optimisation-signal readiness.
•
Use AppsFlyer or an equivalent mobile measurement partner for app campaign setup and analysis, including event mapping, attribution windows, deep links and app-event optimisation.
•
Understand privacy-related app measurement concepts, including SKAdNetwork, and flag material discrepancies between platform, MMP and backend reporting.
Reporting and analysis
•
Run weekly analysis for assigned markets and identify key performance drivers, blockers, risks and opportunities independently.
•
Produce concise reporting covering performance versus target, budget pacing, funnel and quality signals, material changes and planned optimisations.
•
Provide actionable creative, audience, placement, platform and landing-page insights with clear owners and next actions.
•
Use spreadsheets confidently for pivots, lookups, reconciliations and large platform exports.
•
Maintain clear documentation for tests, budget moves, structural changes and material optimisation decisions.
Multi-market delivery and agency QA
•
Execute and optimise multi-market and multi-language campaigns with appropriate consideration of local audience behaviour, creative conventions, copy and compliance nuance.
•
Coordinate translations and local validation where needed; do not rely on unreviewed machine translation for market-facing copy.
•
Turn around agreed ad hoc requests to deadline while protecting planned priorities.
•
QA agency output in assigned markets against agreed build, tracking, creative, compliance and reporting standards.
•
Escalate conflicts in market priority, resource or deadline risk promptly.
Compliance and governance

Monitor and resolve ad and asset disapprovals, escalating policy or legal questions through the correct internal route.
•
Follow approved claims, disclaimers, targeting restrictions, landing-page requirements and market rules, maintaining an auditable record of material changes.
•
Apply disciplined pre- and post-launch QA covering naming, objective, audience, exclusions, placements, budgets, schedule, optimisation event, URLs, tracking, creative and policy status.
Ways of working
•
Communicate proactively with the line manager on progress, blockers, decisions and deadline risk.
•
Organise concurrent market and platform priorities effectively and deliver to agreed timelines.
•
Collaborate with creative, CRO/web, app, analytics, MarTech, compliance and agency partners while retaining clear ownership of paid social execution.
•
Stay current with relevant changes across Meta, TikTok and X, applying new automation and AI-led capabilities only where they support agreed objectives and controls.

•
2+ years of hands-on paid social experience, ideally in a high-competition or complex vertical.
•
Proven day-to-day campaign delivery across Meta, with practical hands-on execution across TikTok and X.
•
Experience managing both web and app acquisition campaigns, including optimisation to conversion and app events.
•
Ability to build, QA, launch, optimise and troubleshoot campaigns independently across concurrent markets.
•
Strong audience-management capability across prospecting, retargeting, first-party/custom audiences, expansion, exclusions and saturation analysis.
•
Ability to analyse creative performance and brief new concepts, iterations and platform-native variations to a creative team.
•
Practical budget pacing and short-term forecasting skills, including early identification of over- or underspend risk.
•
Experience designing and interpreting structured tests across creative, audiences, placements, optimisation and campaign setup.
•
Ability to assess landing-page and post-click performance and brief evidence-based improvements without requiring full CRO ownership.
•
Working knowledge of paid social conversion tracking, event validation and troubleshooting across web and app.
•
Strong performance-analysis and written-reporting skills, with the ability to convert data into prioritised actions.
•
Strong spreadsheet skills, including pivots, lookups, reconciliations and handling large data exports.
•
Disciplined QA and governance approach covering naming, URLs, tracking, audiences, budgets, creative, policy status and change logging.
•
Clear written communication for reporting upwards and briefing internal teams, agencies and external partners.
•
Proactive workload management, ownership of deadlines and early escalation of blockers or risk.
Desirable skills and experience:

Experience advertising financial services or another regulated category across Meta, TikTok or X, including policy restrictions, verification and disapproval resolution.

Experience managing multi-market and multi-language paid social accounts.

AppsFlyer or equivalent MMP experience, including app-event mapping, deep links, attribution windows and SKAdNetwork concepts.

GA4, Looker Studio, Power BI or comparable analytics and reporting experience.
•
Experience supporting conversion-lift, brand-lift or incrementality studies and interpreting results appropriately.
•
Experience using public ad libraries or creative-discovery tools for structured competitor and creative monitoring.
•
Understanding of downstream quality, value-based optimisation or predictive customer-value signals.
•
Experience QAing agency work or coordinating delivery across internal and external partners.
•
Working knowledge of current platform automation and AI-led campaign products, with sound judgement on when to use or constrain them.

Additional Information
Role boundaries:

Payward Services is an enterprise infrastructure platform that enables companies to seamlessly integrate trading, payments, funding, and digital asset services through a single unified system. It provides coordinated liquidity, custody, compliance, risk management, and settlement capabilities, reducing operational complexity for fintechs, banks, brokerages, and payment providers.

As the first dedicated Sales Operations Analyst on the team, you’ll support Business Development across PWS and xStocks so our salespeople can spend their time selling. You’ll run RFP and DDQ responses from start to finish, prepare the team for diligence meetings, qualify and route inbound leads, and keep our CRM, pipeline reporting, and customer insights accurate. You’ll report to PWS sales leadership and work closely with Business Operations, Solutions, Legal, Compliance, and Product.

 


THE OPPORTUNITY

 - Own RFP and DDQ responses for PWS and xStocks from kickoff through submission: triage incoming questions, route technical and compliance items to Solutions and Compliance, and make sure answers are validated before they go out

 - Comfort building simple reports and dashboards

 - Excellent writing, editing, and document formatting skills

 - Clear, confident communication with senior internal stakeholders and external clients

 - Understanding of institutional and B2B sales cycles in financial services

 - Proactive, process-oriented approach, with the ability to identify issues and implement effective solutions

NICE TO HAVES

 - Personal ownership of MariaDB incident diagnosis, performance tuning and tested restore or point-in-time recovery. You can explain what you did, how you established data integrity and what remained uncertain.

 - Clear written technical judgment and demonstrated delivery across teams without reporting-line authority. You help stakeholders make sound database design and lifecycle decisions, and develop experienced engineers through shared delivery.

About the Role

Bybit is seeking a Wallet Operations Manager to join our EU Finance team. The role combines hands-on wallet operations with digital asset management, ensuring secure and efficient asset transfers, settlements, reconciliations, and safeguarding of client crypto assets.

The successful candidate will work closely with Finance, Treasury, Risk, and Technology teams to support daily operations and maintain reliable wallet infrastructure and asset controls.

•

Wallet Operations: Operate and manage hot, warm, and cold wallets, including wallet rebalancing, asset transfers, and transaction approvals.

•

Wallet Infrastructure: Work with institutional custody platforms, including MPC-based wallet solutions, transaction workflows, and wallet configurations.

•

Asset Settlements: Execute and monitor crypto asset settlements, internal transfers, and cross-chain transactions, ensuring timely and accurate processing.

•

Safeguarding: Support the safeguarding and segregation of client crypto assets in accordance with internal policies and regulatory requirements.

•

Asset Reconciliation: Reconcile on-chain wallet balances with internal systems and custody records, identifying and resolving discrepancies.

•

Liquidity Management: Coordinate with Treasury to ensure sufficient asset availability across wallets and networks.

•

Operational Controls: Maintain secure transaction approval workflows, maker-checker controls, and wallet access permissions.

•

Process Improvement: Maintain SOPs, support automation initiatives, and improve the efficiency and reliability of wallet operations.

•

Operational Support: Investigate failed transactions, settlement issues, and other wallet-related incidents, coordinating with internal stakeholders as needed.

•

Support internal and external audits by providing relevant wallet and asset records.

Key Requirements

•

3+ years of experience in crypto wallet operations, digital asset custody, exchange operations, or a related field.

•

Bachelor's degree in Finance, IT, Computer Science, or equivalent practical experience.

•

Strong technical understanding of blockchain networks, wallet infrastructure, private key management, MPC, and multi-signature solutions.

•

Hands-on experience with institutional digital asset custody platforms and wallet management systems.

•

Good understanding of crypto asset transfers, settlements, liquidity management, and blockchain transaction processes.

•

Experience with asset reconciliation, safeguarding, and operational controls.

•

Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with attention to detail.

•

Ability to work independently and collaborate across Finance, Treasury, Risk, and Technology teams.

•

Professional fluency in English; Mandarin Chinese is an huge advantage.

Nice to Have

•

Experience at a cryptocurrency exchange, custodian, or regulated financial institution.

•

Understanding of EU MiCAR safeguarding and segregation requirements.

•

Familiarity with on-chain monitoring tools and blockchain explorers.

•

Experience with process automation or operational reporting.

Join the Pioneer Crypto Brand in the Philippines!
 
Coins is the most established crypto brand in The Philippines and has gained the trust of more than 18 million users. Through the easy-to-use mobile app, users can buy and sell a variety of different cryptocurrencies and access a wide range of financial services.

This is the first compliance hire for our North American businesses: a Canadian and a US money services business in a regulated payments group. You will hold three roles at both entities: Compliance Officer, Risk Officer, and Money Laundering Reporting Officer (MLRO). The job is to build the programs, then run them.
 
Both businesses are early. They move money across borders for business clients, with foreign exchange where needed, and their volumes are starting now. You will work with a small team and can bring in outside providers for monitoring and reviews, working under your direction. You will report to David.


As Compliance Officer (both entities)
• Build, then keep current, each entity's written compliance program, with policies approved by a senior officer: client and beneficial-ownership due diligence, enhanced measures for higher-risk clients, record keeping, travel-rule data and training.

• Assess money laundering, terrorist financing and sanctions-evasion risk across clients, products, delivery channels and geographies, and assess new products, payment rails and corridors before launch.

• Set the outside compliance provider's scope, review its work and sign off what it produces.

• Run the written, ongoing training program and its training plan for staff and anyone acting for the entities.

• Keep each entity's registrations current: the money services business registration with FINTRAC and the payment service provider registration with the Bank of Canada in Canada; the FinCEN registration in the US, renewed every two years and re-filed within 180 days of a triggering change.

• Lead regulator examinations and requests for information, and answer due-diligence requests from banks, payout partners and clients.

• Monitor state money transmission licensing requirements for the US entity's activity, and advise the business before it enters a new state or product.

As MLRO (both entities)
• Run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening, and decide every escalated alert.

• Canada: file suspicious transaction reports with FINTRAC as soon as practicable after reasonable grounds to suspect are established, and terrorist property reports; oversee the prescribed reports, including international electronic funds transfers and virtual currency receipts of C$10,000 or more.

• US: file suspicious activity reports with FinCEN for suspicious transactions of US$2,000 or more within 30 days of initial detection, and keep them with their supporting documents for five years; oversee currency transaction reporting and OFAC blocking and reject reporting.

• Act as the contact for law enforcement requests and production orders, and protect the confidentiality of every report.

As Risk Officer (both entities)
• Canada: act as the senior officer who oversees the written risk management and incident response framework under the Retail Payment Activities Regulations, its incident reports and its third-party risk, and any safeguarding-of-funds framework if end-user funds are held.

• Canada: file the annual report to the Bank of Canada by March 31, and give notice of a significant change or new activity at least five business days before it happens.

• Maintain each entity's risk register and risk appetite, covering compliance, operational, third-party and partner risk, and report it to the board.

• Commission the independent reviews: FINTRAC's effectiveness review at least every two years, the Bank of Canada framework review at least every three years, and the US program's independent review; track every finding to closure.

Must have
• At least 7 years in anti-money-laundering and sanctions compliance at money services businesses, payment companies or the payments arm of a bank, including 3 or more as a compliance officer, MLRO or deputy.

• Deep knowledge of Canada's Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act and FINTRAC's guidance, and working knowledge of the Retail Payment Activities Act.

• Has built a compliance program, not only run one: written its policies, risk assessment and training plan.

• Has decided on and filed suspicious transaction reports, and has run transaction monitoring and sanctions screening.

• Has taken a business through a FINTRAC, bank-partner or audit examination and closed the findings.

• Due diligence on business clients, including clients that pay out for their own customers, and on banks and payout partners.

• A recognised AML certification, such as CAMS, or equivalent experience.

• Writes clearly for boards, regulators and banks, and works alone across time zones.

• Can pass the background checks regulators and banking partners require.

Can be learned here, or nice to have
• The US Bank Secrecy Act, FinCEN reporting and OFAC sanctions. Specialist support is available while you learn the US regime.

• Operational risk and incident response frameworks.

• Cross-border business payments with foreign exchange, or payments funded in stablecoins or other virtual currency, including the travel rule.

• US state money transmission licensing.

• Payout corridors in Asia-Pacific.

• Has managed outsourced compliance providers or set up monitoring and screening tools.

• Has been the officer of more than one entity at once.
